title: YouTube promises custom feeds and a lot more AI later this year
gist: At Made on YouTube, Google announced prompt-built Custom Feeds, GIF comments and group chats, a more prominent Ask YouTube AI with shopping features, Gemini-based creator editing and Ask Studio, plus live stream matchmaking, a monetization-driven Live Showdown, and real-time live autodubbing aimed at the 40% of live watch time from foreign viewers.

insights.claim: YouTube will let US users on web, mobile and TV create multiple Custom Feeds as new tabs by typing a description, then refine them by editing the prompt and rating suggested videos.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Prompt-driven feeds shift recommendation control toward users and could change engagement and ad-targeting dynamics.
insights.locator: The design of YouTube’s homepage feed comes under fire often

insights.claim: YouTube is adding GIFs in comments on videos and Shorts later this year and group chat in direct messages, initially only in the US, UK, Singapore, Brazil and some European countries.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: YouTube is layering social-network features onto video to keep interaction on-platform.
insights.locator: Interacting on YouTube will also change later this year.

insights.claim: Ask YouTube, the AI assistant, is being made more prominent, taking a conversational role in product review videos via typed or voice questions and offering organized video recommendations and product comparison tables in search.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Embedding AI into product reviews and search positions YouTube as a shopping-research surface, a potential commerce and ad revenue lever for Google.
insights.quote: YouTube is probably going to nudge you to chat with a robot more often, too.
insights.locator: YouTube is probably going to nudge you

insights.claim: In YouTube Music, Ask Music is moving to the top of the app where search used to be, can create or edit playlists, and will be joined by an AI 'Your Podcast Lineup' weekly spoken podcast preview, with these AI features limited to YouTube Music subscribers.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Gating AI features behind subscriptions is a tactic to lift paid YouTube Music conversion.
insights.locator: The music version of this AI is also expanding.

insights.claim: Google claims a large majority of US YouTube video posters used AI to create or edit content in the past year, and is adding Gemini-based conversational editing in the YouTube Create app plus A/B testing of up to three video versions.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: High creator AI adoption expands Gemini's distribution and usage inside Google's own ecosystem.
insights.locator: According to Google, YouTube creators are very invested in AI tools.

insights.claim: A new Ask Studio tool will recommend pacing, framing and thumbnails, generate AI thumbnails, and run in the background to analyze older videos and suggest ways to boost their views.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: AI-optimized back catalogs could raise overall watch time and ad inventory without new uploads.
insights.locator: A new tool called Ask Studio

insights.claim: Early next year YouTube will use live matchmaking to merge streams from creators who may not know each other, feeding a Live Showdown feature where streamers compete on a leaderboard for the most chats, gifts and Super Chats.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Gamified tipping competitions are designed to raise viewer spending, boosting YouTube's take from live gifting revenue.
insights.quote: So whoever gets viewers to spend the most money “wins,” essentially. Someone in this equation is probably losing, but it’s not the streamers.
insights.locator: These shared streams will connect to a new feature called Live Showdown

insights.claim: YouTube says 40 percent of live watch time comes from viewers outside the creator's home country, and it will launch real-time live autodubbing early next year, likely built on Google's improved Gemini translation model.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Real-time translation could expand the addressable audience for live content and globalize creator monetization.
insights.locator: The last creator update could make more content accessible
